sentiment.rationale: The expectation baseline is the consensus revenue of $11,966.85mm and EPS of $0.55, which the document explicitly shows were beaten (revenue $12,050.76mm, EPS $0.56). More importantly, management raised forward guidance: 2026 revenue forecast of $51 billion (14% YoY growth) and operating margin of 31.5% (up 2 points), with ad revenue expected to roughly double to ~$3 billion. The tone is confident, with no major risks or hedges flagged. The surprise is the combination of a modest beat and a clear, above-consensus forward outlook, justifying a moderately positive score.

summary.revenue: FQ4 2025 revenue of $12,050.76mm, beating consensus of $11,966.85mm by 0.70%. Full-year 2025 revenue growth of 16%.
summary.eps: FQ4 2025 normalized EPS of $0.56, beating consensus of $0.55 by 1.82%.
summary.guidance: FY 2026 revenue forecast of $51 billion (14% YoY growth). Operating margin guidance of 31.5% (up 2 points, including ~0.5 point drag from expected M&A expenses). Ad revenue expected to roughly double to ~$3 billion in 2026.
summary.margin: Operating margin guidance for 2026 is 31.5%, up 2 points from 2025. Excluding M&A drag, margin expansion is ~2.5 points. In 2025, operating profit grew roughly 30% with expanding margins.
key_risks: Content amortization growth forecast of 10% in 2026 implies acceleration from 2025.
Pending acquisition of Warner Bros. Studios and HBO requires regulatory approvals, though management expressed confidence.
Viewing of second-run licensed titles was lower year-over-year due to reduced volume of licensed titles carried across most regions.
key_opportunities: Ad sales business roughly doubled in 2025 and expected to roughly double again in 2026 to ~$3 billion.
Under 10% of TV time in all major markets, with hundreds of millions of households still to sign up.
Only about 7% of addressable market in terms of consumer and ad spend, indicating massive room for growth.
New initiatives: live events outside U.S. (World Baseball Classic in Japan), video podcasts, cloud-first gaming strategy, and expanded licensing deals (Sony, Universal, Paramount).
Warner Bros. acquisition seen as a strategic accelerant, providing 100 years of IP, a theatrical business, and HBO brand.
